script: At two in the morning on July 30th, 1916, a colossal explosion tore New York Harbor apart, and almost nobody today remembers why it happened. The target was Black Tom Island, a giant munitions depot packed with two million pounds of ammunition waiting to be shipped to the Allies. The blast was so violent that it registered on seismographs like an earthquake and was felt as far away as Philadelphia and Maryland. Red-hot shrapnel screamed across the water and slammed directly into the Statue of Liberty herself. The damage to her raised arm was so serious that her torch has stayed closed to the public from that night all the way to this very day. But here is the secret the newspapers quietly buried in the days that followed: this was no accident at all. German secret agents had slipped into a still-neutral America and set the entire depot ablaze on purpose. The United States was not even in the war yet, and enemy saboteurs were already striking on American soil. It took decades of patient investigation before Germany was finally forced to pay for the entire attack in 1953. And so a deliberate act of war scarred one of America's greatest icons, then quietly vanished from the pages of history.

title: Why the Statue of Liberty's Torch Has Been Closed for 110 Years
description:
July 30, 1916: German saboteurs detonated the Black Tom munitions depot in New York Harbor. The blast hit like an earthquake, shattered windows across Manhattan, and drove shrapnel into the Statue of Liberty. Her torch has been closed to the public ever since. America wasn't even in World War 1 yet.

110 years later, should the Statue of Liberty's torch finally reopen? REOPEN or KEEP IT CLOSED. Say your pick below.
